title: Word Search II
oneLinerQuestion: Find all dictionary words that can be constructed on a 2D character board.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Word Search II problem requires finding all words from a dictionary that can be formed by sequentially adjacent characters on an M x N board. Running individual DFS backtracking searches for every dictionary word leads to redundant traversals and an exponential time blowup. Instead, all target words are indexed upfront into a Trie (Prefix Tree). We then launch a single DFS exploration from each cell of the grid while simultaneously walking down the Trie. If the character path on the grid does not match any prefix branch in the Trie, the search branch is immediately pruned. Storing the full word directly at terminal Trie nodes eliminates string reconstruction and duplicate tracking.

- Step 1: Trie Building & Word Storage — We construct a Trie from the `words` array. Each `TrieNode` contains a `children` map and an optional `word = null` property. When inserting a word, we store the entire string at the terminal node (`node.word = word`) instead of just a boolean flag, allowing direct retrieval upon completion.

- Step 2: Global State & Setup — We initialize a results array `result = []`, determine board dimensions `rows = board.length` and `cols = board[0].length`, and reference the Trie root `root`.

- Step 3: Backtracking DFS Traversal Definition — We define a helper `dfs(r, c, parentNode)`: check boundary conditions `if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols)` and verify if the cell is currently visited or absent in the Trie node's children (`const char = board[r][c]; if (!parentNode.children[char]) return;`).

- Step 4: Word Discovery & De-duplication Pruning — Advance to the child node: `const currNode = parentNode.children[char]`. If `currNode.word !== null`, we have successfully found a dictionary word on the board: push `currNode.word` into `result` and set `currNode.word = null` to prevent duplicate additions.

- Step 5: In-Place Visited Masking & Neighbor Exploration — Temporarily mark the current grid cell to prevent reuse within the same word path (`board[r][c] = '#'`). Recursively invoke `dfs` across all four orthogonal directions: `(r + 1, c)`, `(r - 1, c)`, `(r, c + 1)`, and `(r, c - 1)`. Afterward, restore the cell value (`board[r][c] = char`) during backtracking.

- Step 6: Grid Scan & Trie Optimization — Loop through each cell `(r, c)` of the board and call `dfs(r, c, root)`. Leaf nodes in the Trie can optionally be pruned after discovery to further reduce search space. Once all cells are visited, return `result`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(M * N * 4^(L)) in the worst case, where M * N is the board dimension and L is the maximum word length, heavily mitigated by prefix pruning in the Trie. Space Complexity: O(K * L) auxiliary space to build the Trie for K words of average length L, plus O(L) recursion stack depth during DFS.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION findWords(board, words):
    trie = BUILD_TRIE(words), res = SET(), visited = SET()
    ROWS = LENGTH(board), COLS = LENGTH(board[0])
    FUNCTION dfs(r, c, node, word):
        IF r < 0 OR c < 0 OR r >= ROWS OR c >= COLS OR (r,c) IN visited OR board[r][c] NOT IN node.children THEN RETURN
        ADD (r,c) TO visited; node = node.children[board[r][c]]; word = word + board[r][c]
        IF node.isWord THEN ADD word TO res
        dfs(r+1,c,node,word); dfs(r-1,c,node,word); dfs(r,c+1,node,word); dfs(r,c-1,node,word)
        REMOVE (r,c) FROM visited
    END FUNCTION
    FOR r FROM 0 TO ROWS - 1 DO:
        FOR c FROM 0 TO COLS - 1 DO dfs(r, c, trie.root, '')
    END FOR
    RETURN ARRAY(res)
END FUNCTION
